items.excerpt: VP and GM, Google Search Ads and Ads on Google Experiences We’re bringing ads in AI Mode to new countries. As AI transforms how people search, queries are becoming increasingly conversational. In AI Mode, queries are, on average, three times longer than traditional searches. 1 AI helps us better understand what people are looking for, allowing us to connect them to the businesses and services that best match their needs. Our research shows that people are comfortable with ads in AI Mode and find them highly relevant. In fact, click-through rates are already similar between sponsored and organic product list items within AI Mode. 2 Now we're scaling ads in AI Mode in Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Singapore. In Q4 2026, we plan to expand to additional locales, including Brazil, Mexico, and the United Kingdom. To allow ads in follow-up queries in AI Mode, we are launching multiturn ads in the U.S. Ads will be clearly labeled as “Sponsored.” We’ll continue testing new formats to ensure ads remain helpful and relevant.

items.excerpt: Every eligible ad on Facebook and Instagram is now scored at over 1bn a second per GPU server, 100x the 2024 rate. What sits behind Meta's conversion claim? Meta today published the technical design of the second generation of Andromeda, the system that decides which ads on Facebook and Instagram reach the ranking stage, and claimed it has delivered a 2.4% increase in conversions on Facebook since 2025. According to the company, the rebuilt retrieval engine now scores every eligible ad in its candidate pool at more than one billion ads per second on a single GPU server - a figure Meta describes as a 100x lift over the version it launched in December 2024. Before Meta picks which ad a person sees, a first system quickly shortlists candidates from an enormous pile of ads, and Meta has rebuilt that system so it can check every eligible ad, more than one billion of them every second on one server. That matters to anyone advertising on Facebook or Instagram, because an ad that is not shortlisted never reaches the auction, and Meta says the change has lifted Facebook conversions by 2.4% since 2025. items.excerpt: One in 11 Facebook and Instagram ad files from 509 brands carried AI media, 70% built to look real. Labelling rules in New York and the EU already apply to ads. Resemble AI, a Mountain View company that sells software for detecting synthetic media, on October 22, 2026 published a study that scanned 37,768 image and video files from Facebook and Instagram ads and flagged 3,379 of them as AI-generated or manipulated. That is 8.9%, or roughly one file in 11. Of those 3,379 files, two mentioned AI anywhere in the ad copy. The 21-page document, titled the 2026 Synthetic Advertising Report, draws on ads collected from Meta's public archive in September 2026. It covers 509 companies in 26 industries, from Temu and Wayfair to Lufthansa, Teladoc and Turkish Airlines. According to Resemble AI, 70% of the fakes it labelled were photoreal - built to pass as a real photograph or real video - and 46% showed a person. None of the 971 files checked for provenance metadata carried any. The timing matters for advertisers. items.excerpt: Political spending of $12bn is pushing regional brands off local TV before November 3, as YouTube hit a record 15.8% of US TV time in Nielsen's August Gauge. Every second year, the American advertising market gets a lesson in what happens when a buyer with no interest in price arrives in a hurry. Campaigns do not haggle over a 30-second spot in Milwaukee in the last fortnight before an election; they pay what the station asks, and the station can move a grocery chain out of the slot to make room. With the midterm elections set for Tuesday, November 3, that lesson is being taught again, and this time the brands being pushed aside are fleeing to the streaming services that refuse political money, carrying the price pressure with them. The squeeze on local inventory set the tone for a news cycle that ran from Sunday morning into Monday. Nielsen's August Gauge, examined by PPC Land on Sunday, showed YouTube taking a record share of American television time. Washington's Supreme Court on October 8, 2026 affirmed the dismissal of a class action accusing Seattle Children's Hospital of letting Meta's Pixel record parents' health-related searches, holding that the state's all-party consent wiretap statute protects only communications "between two or more individuals" - and that a person typing into a search box run by an automated corporate server does not meet that test. Three parents said a children's hospital let Meta see what they searched for on its website, and Washington's highest court threw the case out. The judges said the state's wiretap law only covers conversations between people, and typing into a website that answers automatically is not a conversation with a person. More often than not, budgets are also lower. While it’s a challenge, don’t overthink it. Performance Goal If you’re able to optimize for a purchase or lead, you’re at an advantage over many local businesses. Do that. While it’s not easy, by any means, you are at least better able to get Meta to prioritize the action you care about. If you can’t optimize for a conversion, you will probably need to optimize for a top-of-funnel action like reach, ad recall lift, ThruPlay views, or interactions. items.excerpt: For ad buyers, 663 experiments put machine-learning estimates of upper-funnel lift at a median 83%, against a randomized 29%. Which lift figures count as proof? Karan Dhir, a marketing measurement product lead at Genentech who previously held senior product roles at Amazon and Walmart, argued in a Substack essay published on September 9, 2026 that advertising platforms deliver two incompatible kinds of numbers through the same interface. One kind, he wrote, is causal evidence. The other is operational telemetry, and peer-reviewed research built on Facebook's experimentation infrastructure measured the distance between them years ago. A measurement specialist wrote that the ad results platforms show you mix two very different things: real experiments and statistical guesses. Research run on Facebook's data found that the guessing methods often landed far from the experimental answer, frequently several times too high and sometimes too low. What changes is the question asked of every lift number before it moves a budget: did a genuine experiment produce it, or did a model? Six days before the rule takes effect, a free calculator built by a University of Illinois engineering student puts one worked example at $230.40 a month - a number that, read closely, measures something narrower than the rise in a monthly invoice. From October 1, Google will bill small businesses that advertise through its Local Services Ads when someone calls during opening hours, nobody picks up, and the caller waits on the line for more than 20 seconds. That touches plumbers, electricians, roofers and other trades that pay Google per lead and cannot always get to the phone. The account he cites carries 286 live ads against a ceiling of 250, and new ads are delivering regardless. Google has published a Google Ads Help Centre page stating that its invalid traffic filters do not, by themselves, stop bogus submissions from reaching advertisers' lead forms. The page places reCAPTCHA, double opt-in email confirmation and server-side validation on the advertiser's side of what the company calls a shared responsibility. PPC News Feed reported the document on September 17, 2026. Google wrote down that its anti-bot systems mostly judge ad clicks after the ad has already shown, so bots and careless people can still fill in a company's contact form. That matters for any business paying Google to find customers, because junk form entries land in sales lists and can teach Google's automated bidding the wrong lessons. Google now says checking those forms, with tools such as reCAPTCHA and email confirmation links, is partly the advertiser's job. items.excerpt: You can turn off the new creative workflow… Meta started rolling out the new creative workflow in April. Also known as Multimedia Experience, it allows advertisers to provide up to 10 images and videos for a single ad. While I use and have generally been happy with the Multimedia Experience, I know I’m in the minority. Most advertisers hate it, mainly because it’s so buggy. Advertisers have had bugs both with ad creation and reporting using the breakdown by Media. What most of these advertisers don’t understand is that you don’t need to keep dealing with these bugs. You can turn this off and switch to the old way. How to Turn It Off When creating an ad, hover over the Media tooltip. There, you can click a link to “Return to original single media experience.” Even if you switch to single media, you can always hover over the same tooltip to switch back to multimedia if you want to in the future. Switch While You Can Presumably, you won’t be able to do this once the Multimedia Experience is officially launched, but you have an option for now. If you’re experiencing so many bugs that it’s not worth it, just switch back.
